rv.q: It’s a clever experiment in dramatic form that gives the performance a compelling high-wire tension and ramps up the emotional stakes.

Nevertheless, the uncertainty surrounding which path the couple will take, and whether they will ultimately choose to stay together or break up, makes for a tender and insightful examination of how relationships can shift almost imperceptibly and yet with profound consequences.
The play paints a unique portrait of a long-term relationship in the modern world that challenges the notion that, as The Beatles once sang, love is all you need.
Another is that, as not all scenarios are equal, the risk of having overlong sections of teasing chitchat that don’t say much is quite high.

The quixotic approach here taken to text can’t disguise the play’s underlying banality: when it ends, you feel not so much the psychic release accompanying drama at full tilt but, alas, a sense of relief.
Mac Gabhann and Lopez Holden make it so easy to believe these two have built a life together, and hard to imagine either of them walking away from it.
Both fantastic performers, it is the natural way they play against each other and, in fact, the way they play the game, that lifts Attention more than what otherwise may have been a mere gimmick.
Nevertheless, there is something quite haunting about Attention.
A romantic drama that pulses and stings at the whim of the performers.
ATTENTION is funny and touching, and full of recognisable human behaviour.
While there is plenty to enjoy about Attention , the script sadly doesn’t quite live up to its exciting and clever premise.
The problem is, is that the stumbling blocks affecting the pair’s romance are the same ones which make the show such hard work as an audience member.
In 75 minutes this isn’t just a virtuosic miracle of quirky brilliance; but a profound exploration of how loves turns on a moment, a word, a random shuffle.
Overall, the storyline that I saw lacked the depth and context of what had actually occurred between A and B, and for the most part the play felt diluted.
Yet, for all its theatrical flair, I found the dramatic substance somewhat lacking.
The thing is: you can flirt with form and with the rules of theatre, you can gamify the medium, but nothing can replace story.
Not understanding all the rules of engagement was a disadvantage, as I couldn’t fully experience the narrative.

cn.t: Critics find Attention's choose-your-own-adventure format for queer romance inventive, with standout performances praised widely. Reception is mixed—some find the concept thrilling, others feel it underdelivers—but the two leads consistently impress.
